paper_title: PAMI: Part Anchored Motion for Text to Human-Object Interaction Generation

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Text-conditioned full-body human-object interaction (HOI) generation requires synthesizing human motion and object trajectories that match the input text while remaining precisely coordinated over time. Most methods represent the human and object as separate trajectories and predict the global human-object couplings. Learning this complex, dynamically changing relationship implicitly, however, often yields object drift, missed contact, and penetration. We introduce PAMI, a Part-Anchored Motion framework for Interaction generation. Inspired by the classic Hough Transform, our key idea is to localize object motion by letting body-part anchors vote for it: we express object motion relative to multiple body-part anchors and use PamiVAE to learn an interaction latent space, decoding frame-wise weights that aggregate these part-specific votes. Building on this representation, PAMI generates interactions in a coarse-to-fine hierarchy. PamiGen first generates a coarse human-object interaction from text in this structured latent space, and PamiRefiner then recursively resolves fine-grained contact geometry using a hybrid surface-sensing representation, combining long-range probes that capture overall body-part influence with short-range sensors that resolve detailed contacts near the object surface. Experiments on InterAct show that PAMI generates more faithful interactions and more accurate human-relative object motion than previous methods, achieving 14.5% higher contact recall than the previous state of the art. Extensive ablations validate the contributions of both the part-anchored voting representation and hybrid surface-sensing refinement.

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: Humans constantly interact with objects, making the ability to generate humanobject interaction (HOI) cornerstone of physical intelligence and embodied AI, with direct implications for robotics, animation, and AR/VR. Driving this generation from natural language is especially valuable, as text offers an intuitive and scalable interface for specifying the rich space of interactions without motion capture or manual authoring. Text-conditioned full-body HOI generation is however non-trivial: it must produce human motion and an object trajectory that match the text and stay coordinated over time. This makes HOI more than the independent generation of two plausible motions, as small relative errors can produce floating grasp, drifting object, missed contact, or penetration. Most full-body text-to-HOI methods diffuse explicit per-frame human and object states Xu et al. (2023; 2025a); Wang et al. (2026b). In text-to-motion, learned temporal representations have shown that motion can instead be generated in compact latent space (Chen et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2023; Jiang et al., 2023; Li et al., 2024). Recent work HOIMask Ji et al. (2026) is the first to use vector quantized latents for full body interaction. However, it represents interaction as two separate trajectories, which cannot capture the complex human-object relations in latent space. Similarly, most other methods Wang et al. (2026b) also use the separate human-object trajectories as representation and rely on feature exchange Wang et al. (2026b), contact prediction Diller & Dai (2024), or guidance based correction Peng et al. (2023) to reason about the interactions. Some methods explore predicting contact distances Xu et al. (2025a) or weighted combination of multiple predictions based on distances Cha et al. (2024); Xu et al. (2025a). But such feature space based correlation reasoning or hard coded weights is suboptimal as the network needs to reason about the complete object geometry under all dynamic pose transformations and even from body regions that are not affecting the object, making it hard to learn the essential correlations efficiently. In this paper, we ask what representation is suitable for generating interaction motion in latent space while respecting the intricate human-object interaction and contacts? To this end, we introduce PAMI: Part Anchored Motion voting for Interaction motion generation in latent space. We take inspiration from the classic Hough Transform (Ballard, 1981) in computer vision, where global structure that is hard to detect directly is instead localized by letting many local elements each vote for it and taking their consensus, an aggregation that is robust to noise and to irrelevant votes. We cast object motion in the same way: the object pose is the global structure, and the body-part anchors are the local voters. We express object translation relative to each body-part anchor in its local frame, so every anchor votes for where the object should be, and let the decoder predict how strongly each anchor votes per frame. Combining these votes with learned weights forms soft, differentiable Hough aggregation that naturally down-weights parts not involved in the interaction. We embed this representation with PamiVAE, variational autoencoder (VAE), into compact interaction latent that preserves subtle geometric relations yet is easier to generate. Humanobject interaction motion is highly dynamic and complex especially from only text as input. We therefore adopt hierarchical coarse-to-fine design, first recovering an approximate interaction and then resolving its fine-grained contact geometry. In the coarse stage, we train PamiGen, textconditioned generator that produces interaction latents decoded into humanobject motion that captures the text, the overall movement, and the anchor-voted humanobject relation. In the fine stage, PamiRefiner recursively refines this motion through hybrid local geometry sensing: longrange probes capture overall body-part influence, while short-range sensors capture detailed contact in the immediate vicinity of the surface. This decomposition lets latent voting establish the coarse interaction while surface sensing recovers the fine, contact-rich geometry. Experiments on InterAct Xu et al. (2025a) dataset show that our method generates more faithful interaction motions with more accurate object motions relative to the human than prior arts. Notably, PAMI achieves 14.5% higher contact recall than previous state-of-the-art method. Extensive ablations also validate that our part-anchored representation is important to learn meaningful latent space for HOI generation and that our hybrid surface sensing and refinement improves geometric correctness of the generated motions. In summary, our main contributions are: We present PAMI, to our knowledge, the first part-based latent generative framework for text-conditioned full-body HOI motion generation. Our generation is hierarchical from coarse to fine and achieves the best performance on the benchmark and generates highquality interaction motion from text. Our code and model will be publicly released.

sections.title: Preprint
sections.content: We introduce body-part based object voting representation that anchors object motion to body parts and lets anchors vote for object movement via learned weights. This allows efficient generation in latent space while preserving subtle human-object relations, yielding semantically well aligned coarse interaction motion. We design hybrid local surface sensing module to train RefineNet that reasons fine human-object geometry and contacts to improve the coarse interaction motion from latent generation. Trained with mixed data from generation and ground truth, our RefineNet improves not only our latent generation results but also baseline generations zero-shot.

sections.title: 2 RELATED WORK
sections.content: Text-to-HOI and latent motion generation. Text-conditioned interaction generation has been studied for handobject motion (Cha et al., 2024; Christen et al., 2024; Song et al., 2026) and for fullbody humanobject motion. Early full-body methods condition generation on intent or object trajectories (Ghosh et al., 2022; Li et al., 2023b;a); more recent diffusion and related generative models generate interactions from text and incorporate contact, object geometry, or humanobject relation features (Xu et al., 2023; Peng et al., 2023; Diller & Dai, 2024; Wu et al., 2024; Song et al., 2024; Xu et al., 2024; Zeng et al., 2025; Xue et al., 2025; Geng et al., 2025; Li et al., 2025b; Jung et al., 2026; Cai et al., 2026; Wang et al., 2026a; Wu et al., 2025; Di et al., 2026; Zou et al., 2026). HIMO (Lv et al., 2024) handles multiple objects, InterAct (Xu et al., 2025a) introduces marker-based representation and large-scale benchmark, and LIGHT (Wang et al., 2026b) denoises body, hand, and object streams at different paces. Most full-body methods operate directly on per-frame motion states, coupling the human and object through feature exchange, relation or contact prediction, or sampling guidance. LatentHOI (Li et al., 2025a) uses latent diffusion for handobject motion, but does not model full-body interaction. In text-to-motion, learned tokenizers and temporal autoencoders have made generation in compact latent spaces common (Chen et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2023; Jiang et al., 2023; Li et al., 2024; Nazarenus et al., 2026). Whole-body and part-based models further separate the dynamics of different body regions (Lu et al., 2023; Li et al., 2026a). We design novel part-anchored voting representation and embed it into compact latent space for faithful interaction generation. Local and relative object representations. Relative object representations encode humanobject coordination directly (Li et al., 2023b; Zeng et al., 2025). Local modeling also appears in STAR (Osman et al., 2020), which restricts pose-dependent body deformation to sparse joint neighborhoods rather than coupling every joint to the full surface. In HOI generation, InterAct (Xu et al., 2025a) uses vectors from body markers to the nearest object surface and weights relative object-motion guidance by markerobject distance. CG-HOI (Diller & Dai, 2024) predicts object transformations associated with body-surface markers and combines them using contact-distance weights. In both cases, distance determines which human locations influence the object. Dex2HOI (Pratikaki et al., 2026) instead predicts mixture weights for left-wrist-relative, right-wrist-relative, and free object trajectories. Our representation extends this learned composition from wrists to full-body and embed them in latent space. Guidance and refinement for HOI. Physical errors in generated interactions can be addressed during training, sampling, or after generation. Contact-aware losses and auxiliary contact or affordance prediction supervise the generator (Li et al., 2023a; Ma et al., 2024; Peng et al., 2023; Diller & Dai, 2024; Cha et al., 2024; Song et al., 2026; Di et al., 2026), while guidance and relation intervention modify diffusion sampling (Karunratanakul et al., 2023; Wu et al., 2024; Xue et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2026b; Li & Dai, 2025; Li et al., 2026b; Ron et al., 2026). InterDiff (Xu et al., 2023) performs kinematics-informed iterative correction, and OOD-HOI (Zhang et al., 2024b) uses predicted contact regions during diffusion inference. Other work applies optimization Xie et al. (2022; 2023); Lee et al. (2026), learned Zhou et al. (2022); Taheri et al. (2024); Xie et al. (2024); Wang et al. (2026a) or physics-based correction (Zhang et al., 2024a; Xu et al., 2024; 2025b; 2026; Lin et al., 2025). GEARS (Zhou et al., 2024) and GRAFT (YM et al., 2026) use local geometry for handobject synthesis and humanscene fitting, respectively. We follow the widely used hierachical design and use latent generation for coarse and local geometry sensing for fine interaction generation.

sections.title: Preprint
sections.content: Figure 2: Overview of PAMI. Body-part anchors vote for the object motion, and PamiVAE embeds this part-anchored interaction into latent space (Sec. 3.1). Generation then proceeds coarse-to-fine: PamiGen samples coarse interaction from text in the latent space (Sec. 3.2), which PamiRefiner refines in explicit space using hybrid longand short-range surface-sensing probes to sharpen contacts (Sec. 3.3).

sections.title: 3 METHOD
sections.content: Given text prompt c, canonical object mesh M, our goal is to generate human motion xh 1:T and rigid-object trajectory xo 1:T of frames that form one coordinated interaction. We use SMPLH Loper et al. (2015); Romero et al. (2017) to represent human motion. Since the generation must jointly satisfy the text, the human motion, and their fine-grained coupling, we adopt coarse-tofine design, illustrated in Fig. 2. PamiVAE first learns compact interaction latent space built on our part-anchored voting representation (Sec. 3.1). text-conditioned generator PamiGen then produces coarse interaction in this space (Sec. 3.2). Finally, PamiRefiner operates in explicit space and recursively refines this interaction to recover fine-grained contact geometry (Sec. 3.3).

More details can be found in appendix. j,t = {po Refinement network PamiRefiner. The input to our network includes the hybrid probe features Flong,t, Fshort,t, human shape parameter, global 6D human pose and object 6D pose. We use an MLP to extract features and then use transformer to compute attention across all tokens and through time. The prediction heads then output delta updates to the coarse human-object interaction motion decoded from generated latents: δθh, δRh , δth , δRo, δto. Training with mixed data. We train our network to refine both corrupted GT and generated motions, denoted as recovery stream and generation stream respectively. This ensures it learns the error pattern of our latent generator while also maintaining generalization. To obtain recovery stream data, we use our trained VAE to encode ground truth interaction motions, and add temporally smooth noise to the decoded motions. For these kinds of input, the GT motions are available hence we train directly using L2 distance between refined output and GT motions. More details in Sec. B.5. The generation stream refines samples from the latent generator. Since text prompt can admit multiple valid motions, direct supervision against single ground-truth motion is inappropriate. Instead, we optimize geometric objectives targeting motion and geometric quality: Lgen = λcLcontact + λpLpenetration + λsLsupport + λmLsmooth + λnLpreserve. (4)

sections.title: Preprint
sections.content: Here, Lcontact pulls relevant body parts toward the object and reduces slip during contact, while Lpenetration penalizes joints inside the object. Lsupport prevents planted feet from sliding, drifting, or penetrating the ground; Lsmooth regularizes abrupt human and object motion; and Lpreserve discourages unnecessary changes to non-interacting body regions, the root, and object trajectory. All losses are evaluated at each refinement step and averaged over three iterations. At inference, the same feed-forward PamiRefiner is applied recursively for small fixed number of steps. We show in Tab. 3 that our mixed data training is important for more faithful generation. More implementation details are provided in Appendix B.

sections.title: 4 EXPERIMENTS
sections.content: We compare against existing baselines and ablate key components: our method outperforms prior approaches on most metrics, and the ablations confirm the value of each design. PamiRefiner also generalizes zero-shot to interactions produced by other methods, improving their geometry. Experimental and evaluation setup. We conduct experiments on the standard InterAct (Xu et al., 2025a) benchmark and follow LIGHT (Wang et al., 2026b) to report metrics along three dimensions: semantic alignment using R-precision and multimodal distance (MM Dist); motion quality using FID, diversity, and foot-skating ratio (FSR); and interaction geometry using penetration depth (Pene), contact ratio (Contact), and interaction precision, recall, and F1. While LIGHT evaluates the latter three metrics only on hand joints, we report them for both hand and all body joints. Additional metrics are reported in the appendix.

Table 1 shows that our method achieves large improvements in both semantic alignment (R-1) and interaction geometry, particularly in penetration and contact. As shown in Figure 4, LIGHT (Wang et al., 2026b) models human and object motion as separate trajectories, so the object often fails to follow the human (chair, tripod). Our anchor representation directly captures humanobject coupling in compact latent space for coherent generation, while local surface sensing refines interaction geometry. Even on the slender tripod (third row), our model keeps secure, natural grasp without penetration.

sections.title: 4.2 ABLATION STUDIES
sections.content: We ablate the main components of our method along two dimensions: the part-anchored representation and latent structure in Table 2, and the design of PamiRefiner in Table 3.

sections.title: 4.2.1 PART ANCHORED VOTING REPRESENTATION
sections.content: Table 2 evaluates the representation designs after refinement. For fair comparison, each generator variant is paired with PamiRefiner trained on its own outputs. The corresponding coarse generations before refinement are reported in Appendix 7. Together, these evaluations examine whether the advantages of the proposed representation persist after geometric refinement. Part-factored human encoder. We use continuous part-based VAE that encodes each body part into separate latent stream and decodes all jointly. Replacing the part encoders with single full-body encoder, while keeping all else fixed, degrades all metrics (Tab. 2a). The benefit appears already in autoencoder where part factorization lowers reconstruction error by 60.8% (Tab. 6). Part-anchored object motion representation. Our object representation encodes part-anchored trajectories in the object latent and combines them through learned voting. We ablate the design choices to understand the importance of anchors, learned weights, and the coordinate representation of global human and object root trajectories. The performance degrades gradually after removing non-wrist anchors (Tab. 2b) or all anchors (Tab. 2c), indicating the importance of our anchor representation and reasoning anchors beyond hands. Our model predicts dynamic per-frame voting weights to combine anchored predictions, rather than averaging them uniformly (Tab. 2d). This better models the local influence of each anchor on the object motion, leading to better hand and body contacts. We also include the absolute poses of the human and object roots in the representation, placing them in the same coordinate system instead of using the commonly adopted frame-relative root representation (Xiao et al., 2025). As shown in Tab. 2e, all metrics substantially degrade without absolute pose, as errors accumulate independently for the human and object, leading to divergent trajectories. See the supplementary website for qualitative examples.

sections.title: 4.2.2 FINE-GRAINED REFINEMENT
sections.content: Refinement quality. As shown in Rows (a) and (f) of Table 3, applying four PamiRefiner steps substantially improves the interaction geometry of the same coarse generations. It nearly halves penetration, brings Contact closer to the ground-truth distribution, and considerably improves both full-body and hand interaction F1. Meanwhile, R-1 remains stable and FID improves, supporting the role of PamiRefiner as fine geometric generator that preserves the semantics of the generated interaction. See qualitative examples on the supplementary website.

sections.title: 5 CONCLUSION AND LIMITATIONS
sections.content: We presented PAMI for text-conditioned full-body HOI generation. Following the HoughTransform idea, we represent object motion as votes from body-part anchors and learn per-frame weights that aggregate the relevant votes, and we generate the interaction in compact part-based latent space. Generation is coarse-to-fine: PamiGen produces coarse interaction in this latent space, and PamiRefiner then refines local interaction poses from hybrid surface geometry sensing. On InterAct, PAMI achieves best performance in almost all metrics, achieving 14.5% higher contact recall than the previous art, and our ablations confirm that the part-based latent, anchor voting, learned weights, and PamiRefiner each contribute. PamiRefiner further improves LIGHT and InterAct outputs without retraining. Our code and models will be publicly released.

sections.title: B IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS
sections.content: B.1 MOTION REPRESENTATION AND COORDINATES Motion is processed at 30 fps in windows of at most 300 frames. For each sequence, the human root in the first frame defines the world coordinate frame, and all subsequent global human and object motion is expressed relative to this frame. We follow MotionStreamer (Xiao et al., 2025) for the 272-dimensional body representation, but replace its frame-relative root variables with global root orientation and translation in this first-frame coordinate system. The remaining features contain root-relative joint positions and velocities, and parent-relative 6D rotations. The two hands are represented separately by wrist-local positions and parent-relative 6D rotations for 15 finger joints per side. PamiVAE uses eight causal body-part encoders for the root, torso, left/right arms, legs, and hands. The object encoder receives its global 6D rotation, free translation, and anchor-relative offsets. All encoders downsample time by four and produce 16-dimensional tokens. Six spatiotemporalattention layers exchange information across tokens and time. One joint human decoder fuses all body-part tokens, and two upsampling stages restore the original frame rate. Table 6 compares VAE reconstruction quality, while Table 7 reports the corresponding generators before refinement. B.2 ANCHOR VOTING IMPLEMENTATION The representation uses five body-part anchorsthe root, left/right wrists, and left/right ankles and one free anchor. Each body-part vote transforms decoded relative offset through its decoded human anchor; the free vote predicts object translation directly. The voting target (cid:101)wt assigns weight to body parts within 1 cm of the object. Multiple active votes are normalized; when no body-part contact is detected, the free branch receives the full vote. We use Lw = MSE(wt, (cid:101)wt) with weight 0.01. At inference, the decoder predicts the votes and softmax weights without the target. Object orientation is decoded separately in 6D. Table 8 reports the additional metrics for the refined representation ablations.

B.3 PAMIGEN: TEXT-CONDITIONED LATENT INTERACTION GENERATION The latent grid contains eight human-part tokens and one object token per latent step. The transformer has 10 layers, width 512, eight attention heads, and feed-forward width 2048. It applies self-attention to the full token grid and cross-attention to frozen caption features. Rotary embeddings encode time, while token embeddings distinguish body parts and the object. The object token is additionally conditioned on basis-point-set features of the canonical mesh (Prokudin et al., 2019). All normalization statistics are computed on the training split; human statistics are computed separately for each part token. To prevent the object loss from being diluted by the larger number of human-part tokens, we compute the human and object errors separately: LRF = Eτ,ϵ (cid:104)(cid:13) (cid:13)vh θ v,h(cid:13) 2 2 + λo vo (cid:13) θ v,o 2 (cid:105) . (5) We use classifier-free guidance with scale 2.5 and 50 integration steps. Decoded losses use Huber distance and are applied only for 0.1 < τ < 0.5. The free-position, free-velocity, and composed translation terms each have weight 5.0; alignment has weight 2.5. Alignment is evaluated only on frames with an active body-part vote, after removing the predicted free weight and renormalizing the remaining weights. Targets come from decoding the clean latent with the same VAE. The object token contains object pose; the global token contains root pose and 16D body-shape feature. Long-range probes use 512 surface points. Short-range probes use separate 16,384-point area-weighted surface sample. For each finger joint and fingertip, we encode at most 64 points within 4 cm using shared pointwise network and masked-mean pooling. Empty neighborhoods produce zero features. Both probe types are recomputed after every refinement step. Features are projected to width 256 and processed by four spatialtemporal transformer blocks. Zero-initialized heads predict bounded updates to joint rotations, root motion, and object SE(3). Training backpropagates through three-step rollout. Object updates are capped at 5 cm and 10; root updates at 10 cm and 5 in yaw. Table 9 reports the complete cross-generator transfer metrics. B.5 PAMIREFINER TRAINING LOSSES Recovery and generation batches alternate 1:1 while the VAE and generator remain frozen. recovery input is corrupted VAE round trip, supervised by the original interaction. We sample clean, root, lower-body, object, and mixed groups with probabilities 0.2/0.1/0.1/0.2/0.1/0.2/0.1; mixed corruption combines two or three groups. torso, upper-body, Temporal noise follows an OrnsteinUhlenbeck process with α 0.895. Root noise is 4.7 cm in xz, 3 in yaw, and 4 cm height offset. Rotation ranges are 25 for the torso, 37 for hips/knees, 25 for ankles, 312 for the upper body, and 415 for fingers. Object noise uses 14 cm translation and 312 rotation. Persistent biases are 16 for the upper body, 28 for fingers, and 15 cm/315 for the object. The corruption distribution is fixed across the three training steps; generated samples are precomputed. The implementation terms follow the five groups in Eq. 4. Lcontact contains surface attraction and contact slip; Lpenetration penalizes humanobject intersection; Lsupport constrains planted feet, ground penetration, and lower-body drift; Lsmooth penalizes abrupt motion and updates; and Lpreserve protects non-interacting body regions, the root, and the object. The five group weights λc, λp, λs, λm, λn are all 1; their internal coefficients and the separate recovery-stream weights are reported in Table 11. Contact masks and segment anchors are computed once from the coarse generation and kept fixed during recursion. Table 10 reports the additional metrics for the RefineNet ablations. Parameter counts, optimizer schedules, and the scalar loss weights are listed in Table 11, read directly from the final checkpoints recorded configurations.

sections.title: C LIMITATIONS AND FUTURE WORK
sections.content: Our experiments focus on the single-human, single-rigid-object setting of InterAct, and the method assumes access to known canonical object mesh for shape conditioning and surface sensing, which may limit its applicability when accurate object geometry is unavailable. Moreover, PamiRefiner is designed as bounded local corrector: it can improve contact when the coarse interaction is already reasonable, but cannot recover from an incorrect action, severe temporal misalignment, or large trajectory error. Future work will extend the framework to interactions involving multiple objects and improve its generalization to novel object shapes beyond those observed during training.
